de-rlp-410102.atlas_note: Bernkasteler Doctor: tiny, very steep site right above Bernkastel. Legend says its wine cured the Archbishop of Trier, Boemund II, in the 14th century. Among the most expensive vineyard land in Germany.

de-rlp-410307.atlas_note: Brauneberger Juffer: long south-facing slope opposite Brauneberg, historically one of the most valued sites of the Mosel. Juffer-Sonnenuhr is its core.

de-rlp-410308.atlas_note: Brauneberger Juffer-Sonnenuhr: the steepest, central part of the Juffer slope, with a sundial among the vines.

de-rlp-410416.atlas_note: Piesporter Goldtröpfchen: south-facing amphitheatre of slate around Piesport, giving rich, fruity Riesling.

de-rlp-410503.atlas_note: Graacher Himmelreich: large, steep slate slope between Bernkastel and Wehlen, known for elegant Riesling.

de-rlp-410506.atlas_note: Wehlener Sonnenuhr: steep slate slope across the Mosel from Wehlen, named after the sundial painted on a rock among the vines. One of the most famous Riesling sites in the world.

de-rlp-410921.atlas_note: Erdener Treppchen: named after the steps carved into the slope to reach the terraces. Red and blue slate.

de-rlp-410947.atlas_note: Ürziger Würzgarten: spectacularly steep site with an unusual red soil, very different from the grey slate around it. Known for spicy Riesling.

de-rlp-511124.atlas_note: Niederhäuser Hermannshöhle: steep site above the Nahe with a mix of slate, porphyry and volcanic rock. A reference Riesling site of the Nahe.

de-rlp-511147.atlas_note: Schlossböckelheimer Felsenberg: volcanic rock site next to Kupfergrube on the Nahe.

de-rlp-511151.atlas_note: Schlossböckelheimer Kupfergrube: terraced site on a former copper mine, planted in the early 20th century by the Prussian state domain.

de-rlp-511319.atlas_note: Monzinger Halenberg: steep blue slate and quartzite site in the upper Nahe.

de-rlp-720105.atlas_note: Niersteiner Ölberg: Roter Hang site above Nierstein, red soil, warm exposure.

de-rlp-720704.atlas_note: Niersteiner Hipping: part of the Roter Hang north of Nierstein, on red Rotliegend soil above the Rhine.

de-rlp-720705.atlas_note: Niersteiner Pettenthal: steep part of the Roter Hang right above the Rhine, on red slate-like soil from the Permian (Rotliegend).

de-rlp-730115.atlas_note: Westhofener Kirchspiel: amphitheatre of limestone and marl in Westhofen, a neighbour of Morstein.

de-rlp-730116.atlas_note: Westhofener Morstein: limestone-rich site in the hills of southern Rheinhessen, famous for powerful dry Riesling.

de-rlp-730205.atlas_note: Dalsheimer Hubacker: limestone site in Flörsheim-Dalsheim, southern Rheinhessen.

wineries: Weingut Oekonomierat Johann Geil I. Erben GbR

communes: Birkweiler, Landau i. d. Pfalz, Siebeldingen
Ilbesheim b. Landau/Pf, Landau i. d. Pfalz

de-rlp-820812.atlas_note: Forster Jesuitengarten: neighbour of Kirchenstück in Forst, once owned by the Jesuits.

de-rlp-820813.atlas_note: Forster Kirchenstück: small site behind the church of Forst, often ranked as the finest in the Pfalz. Basalt, limestone and sandstone in a warm, sheltered spot.

de-rlp-820815.atlas_note: Forster Pechstein: site named after the dark basalt in its soil, from an old volcanic outcrop above Forst.

de-rlp-820816.atlas_note: Forster Ungeheuer: famous Forst site whose name means 'monster', with basalt and limestone soils.

communes: Forst an der Weinstr., Friedelsheim, Wachenheim a.d.Weinstr

wineries: Weingut Oekonomierat Johann Geil I. Erben GbR
